summary: SpaceX's June 2026 IPO (SPCX, $75 billion raised, about $2 trillion value) made the space trade public, and nearly every other space business depends on its launch prices. The fastest real money is Starlink broadband and defense: Golden Dome and spy agencies are the main buyers of satellites, sensors and space data. Lunar landers and in space factories have real contracts and venture money but remain small, government led and slower than promised.

innovations.name: Reusable heavy launch
innovations.what: Rockets whose boosters, and later upper stages, land and fly again. Fully reusable giants like Starship aim to cut the cost per kilogram to orbit by ten times or more, which makes everything else in space cheaper.
innovations.stage_why: Partly reusable Falcon 9 is already the workhorse of the industry. Fully reusable heavy lift is still in testing: Starship V3 first flew on May 22, 2026, but has not yet caught a ship or transferred fuel in orbit. Challengers Neutron and New Glenn are years behind SpaceX.

evidence.cost: Rocket Lab plans about $50 million per Neutron launch for 13 to 15 tonnes to low orbit. SpaceX has not published a Starship price; the goal of much lower cost per kg is unproven.
evidence.approvals: FAA launch licenses gate each Starship flight; after the V3 debut SpaceX needs FAA clearance for the next flight. Space Force national security launch certification decides who wins defense missions.
evidence.money: SpaceX raised $75 billion in the largest IPO ever, pricing at $135 and listing as SPCX on Nasdaq on June 12, 2026; it closed day one at $161.11, about $2.1 trillion in value. Rocket Lab signed 5 Neutron contracts in Q1 2026 before its first flight.
evidence.revenue: SpaceX had 2025 revenue of about $18.7 billion with a GAAP net loss of about $4.9 billion, and lost about $4.3 billion in Q1 2026 (S-1 summaries). Rocket Lab signed 36 new launch contracts in Q1 2026, 31 for Electron.

spreads_to.use: Cheap launch makes large broadband constellations affordable
Rapid launch of Golden Dome sensors and interceptors
Orbital data centers only work if launch cost falls a lot
Starship refueling is required for crewed Moon landings

innovations.bottleneck: Launch capacity itself, controlled by SpaceX, which flies the large majority of US launches. Below that: rocket engines, carbon composite and aluminum lithium structures, and launch pad and range slots at Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg.

next_milestone.event: Next Starship V3 flight with long orbital stay, then a ship to ship propellant transfer test; Neutron first launch
next_milestone.timing: Orbital stay targeted in 2026; Neutron Q4 2026 at the earliest

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if Starship cannot show orbital refueling by the end of 2027, or if launch prices stop falling because SpaceX faces no real competitor.

innovations.name: Satellite broadband and direct to phone
innovations.what: Thousands of low orbit satellites that sell home, ship, plane and military internet, and newer satellites that connect straight to normal phones with no dish.
innovations.stage_why: Starlink is a mass market product with about 10 million subscribers by early 2026. Direct to phone service is earlier, at beta and early adoption: AST SpaceMobile had 13 satellites in orbit and was running carrier beta tests in 2026.

evidence.cost: Starlink earns about $81 per user per month (S-1 based estimates). AST's BlueBird 6 is the largest commercial array in low orbit, designed for 120 Mbps peak speeds.
evidence.approvals: Spectrum licenses from the FCC and foreign regulators are the gate. SpaceX bought EchoStar spectrum (2025) to expand direct to cell. Amazon Leo reached the coverage level for commercial service on July 2, 2026.
evidence.money: SpaceX raised $75 billion at IPO, much of it to fund Starlink and compute. Amazon has launched about 394 Leo satellites. AST has funded its build with repeated stock and convertible sales.
evidence.revenue: Starlink revenue was about $11.4 billion in 2025, 61% of SpaceX revenue. AST guides 2026 revenue of $150 to $200 million and booked $14.7 million in Q1 2026.

spreads_to.use: In flight and at sea internet
Military communications, Starshield for the Pentagon
Fill rural dead zones for phone users through AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile
Connected cars and trucks in remote areas

innovations.bottleneck: Usable radio spectrum and launch capacity. SpaceX controls both the leading constellation and most launch supply, and the spectrum it bought from EchoStar.

next_milestone.event: AST commercial service start with US carriers; Amazon Leo service ramp in the US and Europe

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if Starlink subscriber growth stalls with falling price per user, or if AST cannot start paid commercial service before raising more equity.

innovations.name: Earth observation and space data
innovations.what: Fleets of small imaging and radar satellites that photograph the whole planet often, plus AI software that turns images into alerts for militaries, farmers, insurers and governments. Missile tracking from space is the defense version.
innovations.stage_why: Revenue is real and growing fast, mostly from governments: Planet's revenue rose 58% to a record $116.1 million in the quarter ended July 31, 2026. Commercial buyers are still a minority.

evidence.approvals: Satellite imaging needs NOAA remote sensing licenses. Defense data sales go through the NRO and NGA, and Golden Dome space based interceptor prototypes run on Space Force agreements.
evidence.money: Golden Dome is expected to cost about $185 billion, with first capability by 2028. Space Force awarded agreements worth up to $3.2 billion combined to 12 companies including SpaceX, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Anduril and Raytheon for space based interceptor prototypes (late 2025 to April 2026).
evidence.revenue: Planet backlog about $814.9 million, about half due in 12 months, with adjusted EBITDA of $13.9 million in fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter to July 31, 2026). BlackSky holds NRO contracts (sizes unverified this session).

spreads_to.use: Daily monitoring of troops, ships and missile sites
Crop health and yield estimates
Damage checks after storms and fires
Watching oil storage, mines and pipelines

innovations.bottleneck: Government budgets and security clearances. A few agencies (NRO, NGA, Space Force) are the big buyers, and classified work limits who can compete. Launch slots and ground station access come second.

next_milestone.event: Golden Dome architecture contract awards and Planet fiscal Q3 2027 results
next_milestone.timing: Awards through 2026 to 2028; Planet results early December 2026

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if Golden Dome or NRO commercial imagery budgets are cut in the FY2027 appropriations, since government is most of the revenue.

innovations.name: In space manufacturing, servicing and orbital compute
innovations.what: Factories, repair and refueling robots, private space stations and data centers that work in orbit. Examples: making drug crystals in zero gravity, docking with old satellites to extend their life, and running AI chips on solar power in orbit.
innovations.stage_why: Missions are flying and landing, but revenue is small and mostly government or research. Varda has completed reentry missions (W-5 in January 2026, W-6 in May 2026), and Starcloud flew the first data center GPU in orbit in November 2025. No product made in space is on the market yet.

evidence.approvals: Reentry capsules need FAA reentry licenses and landing rights (Varda lands in Australia). NASA's Commercial LEO Destinations Phase 2 will pick private stations to replace the ISS, with about $1.5 billion across awards.
evidence.money: Starcloud raised $250 million at a $2.3 billion value on August 21, 2026 ($450 million total), with Nvidia and Cisco as new investors. Varda raised a $251 million Series D, $598 million total. SpaceX filed with the FCC for a very large orbital compute constellation (details unverified this session).
evidence.revenue: Very little. Astroscale won a $25.5 million Space Systems Command refueling contract (date unverified this session). Redwire sells in space manufacturing payloads and is a partner on Vast's Haven-1.

spreads_to.use: Growing purer drug crystals in microgravity
Solar powered compute in orbit without grid limits
Refueling and moving military satellites
Making ultra pure crystals and fibers in zero gravity

innovations.bottleneck: Cheap, frequent launch and return capacity, which SpaceX mainly controls. For stations, the scarce input is NASA's anchor tenant money after the ISS retires around 2030.

next_milestone.event: NASA Commercial LEO Destinations Phase 2 awards; Vast Haven-1 launch
next_milestone.timing: Awards expected 2026 to 2027 (timing unverified); Haven-1 no earlier than Q1 2027

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if no space made product finds a paying commercial buyer by 2028 and NASA delays private station funding.

innovations.name: Lunar and cislunar infrastructure
innovations.what: Landers, rovers, relay satellites and power systems for the Moon, paid for mostly by NASA's Artemis program and commercial delivery contracts.
innovations.stage_why: Commercial landers have reached the Moon and NASA pays real contracts, but crewed landing has slipped. Artemis II flew around the Moon in April 2026, while Artemis III was changed to a 2027 low Earth orbit docking test because neither Starship nor Blue Moon landers are ready before late 2027.

evidence.approvals: NASA contracts are the approval: Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) task orders, Human Landing System awards to SpaceX and Blue Origin, and the Lunar Terrain Vehicle program, a potential $4.6 billion award.
evidence.money: Intuitive Machines closed its $800 million purchase of Lanteris (formerly Maxar Space Systems) in Q1 2026. Firefly backlog is about $1.3 billion. NASA Artemis II launched April 1, 2026 and returned safely.
evidence.revenue: Intuitive Machines guides $900 million to $1 billion of 2026 revenue after the Lanteris deal. Firefly booked record Q1 2026 revenue of $80.9 million and guides $420 to $450 million for 2026.

spreads_to.use: Lunar relay and navigation satellites
Small fission reactors for lunar bases (NASA fission surface power)
Long term, water ice and helium-3 prospecting
Watching the space between Earth and the Moon

innovations.bottleneck: NASA funding and a working heavy lander. Starship HLS (SpaceX) and Blue Moon (Blue Origin) are the only crew landers, and both depend on orbital refueling that is unproven.

next_milestone.event: NASA Lunar Terrain Vehicle award and Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 2 to the far side
next_milestone.timing: LTV award pending; Blue Ghost 2 date unverified

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Thesis breaks if NASA's budget cuts CLPS and Artemis further, or if orbital refueling slips crewed landings past 2029.
